questions: Did you sustain any recent head or spinal injury before experiencing this difficulty walking?
Have you noticed numbness, tingling, or weakness in your legs or upper limbs?
Do you experience balance issues even when you are standing still without moving?
Did you have any recent viral or bacterial infection (such as influenza, respiratory infection) before these symptoms began?
Is there a family history of neurological disorders (like multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, or hereditary neuropathy)?
Have you noticed that your walking difficulty varies or fluctuates - sometimes better, sometimes worse?
Have you experienced any significant psychological stress, anxiety, or emotional difficulties recently?
Has anyone else noticed that your gait pattern seems inconsistent with your strength?
Do you have any pain in your hips, knees, back, or legs when you walk?
Are you taking any medications regularly?
How long have you had this difficulty walking?
Can you describe exactly what feels wrong when you try to walk - is it pain, weakness, stiffness, or something else?
When exactly did you first notice this walking difficulty - was it sudden or gradual?
What specifically does it feel like - do your legs feel unstable, uncoordinated, weak, or like they might give way?
What is the exact reason you started using crutches - did a doctor prescribe them?
Did a doctor tell you that you needed crutches?
How long ago did you start using the crutches?
Were the crutches given to you by someone else at this hospital?
Has anyone examined you yet and told you what is wrong?
Have you noticed any problems with your memory or thinking recently?
Have you had any changes in your bladder control - like needing to urinate more frequently or accidentally leaking?
Have you had any problems with your vision - blurry vision, double vision, or difficulty seeing things clearly?
Do you drink alcohol? If yes, approximately how much and how often?
Has this walking difficulty been getting worse gradually over months or years?
Do you notice you are more unsteady when walking in the dark or with your eyes closed?
orders: Bedside examination: Test lower limb muscle strength (hip flexion, knee extension, ankle dorsiflexion, ankle plantarflexion) - Manual Muscle Testing
Bedside examination: Assess deep tendon reflexes in both lower limbs (knee jerks, ankle jerks)
Bedside examination: Test vibration sense and proprioception at the great toes and ankles
Bedside examination: Perform Romberg's test (standing with feet together, eyes open then closed)
Bedside examination: Hoover's sign - ask patient to lie supine, test hip extension on one side while feeling for involuntary contralateral hip flexion
Bedside examination: Observe gait without crutches - ask patient to put crutches aside and walk down the corridor
Bedside examination: Test arm_ROM testing - check for inconsistency between tested strength on formal examination versus functional tasks (e.g., grip strength when "distracted")
served: MRC power in all four limbs
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses
observation for excessive slowness or uneconomic posture
distractibility testing (complex motor task with the unaffected side)
